chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who has a large estate, and when it is the day of al-Mihrjan or al-Nayrouz, they gift him something; they are not doing so to draw near to him with that. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Are they not among the praying ones?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'Then let him accept their gift and reciprocate, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If a shoulder (cut of meat) were gifted to me, I would accept it, and that was from the religion; and if a disbeliever or a hypocrite were to gift me a wasq, I would not accept it, and that was from the religion. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refused to me the scum of the polytheists and the hypocrites, and their food.'

key_terms.كُرَاعٌ: A shoulder or cut of meat
key_terms.مُصَلِّينَ: Praying ones (referring to People of the Book)
key_terms.وَسْقاً: A wasq, a unit of volume/measure

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a Muslim to accept gifts from non-Muslims during their festivals?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of accepting gifts from Ahl al-Kitab during their festivals, provided they are not specifically offered as an act of religious devotion to their idols, thereby distinguishing between social courtesy and religious syncretism. It highlights the Prophet’s pragmatic approach to interfaith relations, where the nature of the gift (e.g., a tool versus food) and the giver's status determine its acceptability, reflecting the Shia principle of maintaining social harmony while preserving theological distinctiveness.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al Karkhy who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happened to have a big place for him. So whenever it was the day of Al-Mihrjaan or Neyrouz, they would gift him something. It was not upon them (to do so) but they wanted to be closer to him with that’. 
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Are they not from the Praying ones?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let him accept their gifts, and suffice them, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘(Even) if a limb of an animal was to be gifted to me<sup>saww</sup>, I<sup>saww</sup> would accept it, and that was always from the Religion; and if an Infidel or a hypocrite were to gift to me<sup>saww</sup> a load, I<sup>saww</sup> would not accept it, and that was always from the Religion. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Refused to me<sup>saww</sup> the scum of the Polytheists and the hypocrites, and their meals’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from all from ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al- Karkhiy who has said the following:

“I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who possesses a great deal of goods. On the times of festivities or the day of Nawroz, they give him as gifts which they did not have to give him but they wanted to become nearer to him. He (the Imam) asked, ‘Are they not the ones who perform prayers?’ I (the narrator) replied, ‘Yes, they perform prayer.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He must accept their gift and reciprocate. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “Even if a foot of sheep is given to me as a gift I accept it. It is part of the discipline of religion. On the other hand, if an unbeliever or hypocrite gives me as gift, a whole load of goods, I do not accept. It is of the discipline of religion. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, disdains my accepting gifts of unbelievers and hypocrites.’””
